question: Does a class-conditional, quality-filtered synthetic generator give a downstream classifier more test accuracy than standard image augmentation when only a few real labeled examples per class are available?
method: 15 real images/class; baseline = 10x shift/rotate/noise augmentation + MLP; improved = per-class shrinkage Gaussian in PCA space, filtered by logistic-regression confidence >= 0.8, same MLP; seeds 42-44.
baseline: Standard augmentation generator (random shifts, small rotations, pixel noise; 10 synthetic per real image) with an MLPClassifier trained on real + synthetic.
improved: Class-conditional Gaussian generator in PCA space with Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage, same number of samples before filtering, kept only if a logistic regression trained on real images assigns the intended class probability >= 0.8; same MLPClassifier.
notes: Digits are a stand-in for document character crops, not the paper's VLM/diffusion pipeline. Hyper-parameters were fixed a priori (no tuning, so no test-set selection; no CV search was needed). Three seeds (42-44) per the mandated protocol. The filter classifier is trained only on the same real images. Std values are population std across seeds and are based on very few runs.
